terms.meaning: Complete physical, mental and social well-being, not just the absence of disease.
What the patient feels, such as pain or tiredness.
What others can see or measure, such as fever or a rash.
A germ that causes disease: a bacterium, virus, fungus, protozoan or worm.
A disease caused by pathogens, which can spread to other people.
A disease that does not spread from person to person, such as diabetes.
The body’s natural ability to fight disease.
An insect that spreads pathogens, such as a mosquito or housefly.
A disease that lasts for a long time, more than 3 months.
A medicine that kills or stops the growth of bacteria.

items.name: Tuberculosis
items.formula: Caused by bacteria. It affects the lungs.
items.example: Cough, fever, tiredness and night sweats.

items.name: Common cold and flu
items.example: Coughs and sneezes spread them, so cover your mouth.

items.name: Chickenpox and measles
items.formula: Caused by viruses. Both give a skin rash and fever.

items.name: Cholera
items.formula: Caused by bacteria. It causes diarrhoea and dehydration.
items.example: Boiled water and properly cooked food help to prevent it.

items.name: Typhoid
items.formula: Caused by bacteria. It gives fever and affects the intestine.
items.example: Boiled water helps to prevent it.

items.name: Hepatitis A
items.formula: Caused by a virus. It affects the liver and can give jaundice.

items.name: Roundworm (ascariasis)
items.formula: Worms live in the small intestine and feed on nutrients.
items.example: It can cause anaemia and poor growth.

items.name: Malaria
items.formula: Caused by protozoa, spread by mosquitoes.
items.example: High fever with sweating and chills.

items.name: Dengue
items.formula: Caused by a virus, spread by mosquitoes.
items.example: Pain in the muscles and joints.

items.name: Stopping mosquitoes
items.formula: Do not let water stand in pots or tyres.

items.name: Scurvy
items.example: Citrus fruits help to prevent it.

items.name: Goitre
items.example: Iodised salt helps to prevent it.

items.name: Anaemia
items.formula: Lack of iron or vitamin B12.
items.example: Worms in the intestine can also cause anaemia.

items.name: Diabetes
items.formula: A lifestyle-linked disease with frequent urination, great thirst and slow healing.
items.example: Diet and exercise help to manage it.

items.name: How vaccines work
items.formula: They train the immune system with dead, weakened or harmless parts of a germ.
items.example: The body learns to fight the germ without getting the disease.

items.name: Edward Jenner
items.formula: Made the first vaccine, against smallpox.
items.example: He saw that milkmaids who had mild cowpox did not get smallpox.

items.name: Alexander Fleming
items.formula: Found penicillin, the first antibiotic, in 1928, from the mould Penicillium.
items.example: The mould stopped bacteria growing on his dish.

items.name: Antibiotic resistance
items.formula: Careless use lets surviving bacteria multiply, and then the medicine stops working.
items.example: Finish the course that the doctor gives.

mistakes.text: Antibiotics do not work on viruses, so they will not cure a cold or dengue.
A fever can be measured, so it is a sign. A headache is only felt, so it is a symptom.
Mosquitoes carry malaria but do not cause it. The cause is a protozoan.
Diabetes is not caught from another person. It is not caused by a germ.
